scenarios.name: Empty name string is rejected by Zod min(1)
scenarios.oracle: Name is a required NOT NULL varchar(255) field. An empty string must fail Zod validation with 'Name is required' and never reach the API.
actions: Fill all other required fields (unitDefinitionId, itemType)
verify: Zod validation rejects with 'Name is required'
No fetch call is made to /api/items
Form displays field-level error on name

scenarios.name: Whitespace-only name passes Zod min(1) — it is NOT trimmed
scenarios.oracle: The name field uses z.string().min(1), not nullableString. Whitespace-only strings like '   ' have length > 0 and PASS validation. The untrimmed string reaches the database.
verify: Zod validation passes — min(1) checks length, not content
Payload contains name: '   ' (untrimmed whitespace)
The API receives the whitespace string and passes it to DAL

scenarios.name: Empty/whitespace SKU is normalized to null by nullableString
scenarios.oracle: nullableString trims the input and converts empty results to null. Whitespace-only or empty string SKUs must become null in the payload, not empty string.
verify: Zod transforms SKU to null (trim + empty → null)
Payload sent to API has sku: null
DB receives NULL for sku column — partial unique index is not triggered

scenarios.name: SKU longer than 50 chars passes Zod but may fail at DB
scenarios.oracle: Zod has NO max length check for SKU. A string longer than 50 characters passes schema validation and reaches the database, where varchar(50) will reject it with a Postgres error.
actions: Enter a 51-character string in SKU field
verify: Zod validation passes — no maxLength constraint
API sends the 51-char string to DAL
Postgres rejects with 'value too long for type character varying(50)' or truncates
API returns a 500 error (unhandled DB constraint violation)

scenarios.name: Category longer than 100 chars passes Zod but may fail at DB
scenarios.oracle: Zod has NO max length check for category. A string longer than 100 characters passes schema validation and reaches the database, where varchar(100) will reject it.
actions: Type a 101-character string into the category combobox
Select the '+ Create' option to use it
verify: Zod validation passes — no maxLength constraint
API sends the 101-char category to DAL
Postgres rejects with varchar(100) constraint violation

scenarios.name: Non-numeric purchase price passes Zod and fails at Postgres
scenarios.oracle: defaultPurchasePrice uses nullableString, which only trims and null-converts. There is NO numeric validation. A string like 'abc' passes Zod and is sent as a string to Postgres numeric(10,4), which rejects it.
verify: Zod validation passes — nullableString only trims, 'abc' is non-empty so it stays
Payload contains defaultPurchasePrice: 'abc'
Postgres rejects: invalid input syntax for type numeric
API returns 500 error

scenarios.name: Selling price exceeding numeric(10,2) precision fails at DB
scenarios.oracle: defaultSellingPrice is numeric(10,2). A value like '99999999999' (11 digits) exceeds the precision and will fail at the DB level. Zod performs no numeric or range validation.
verify: Zod validation passes
Payload contains defaultSellingPrice: '99999999999'
Postgres rejects: numeric field overflow for numeric(10,2)

scenarios.name: Empty safety stock is transformed to '0' by Zod
scenarios.oracle: safetyStock uses z.string().transform(v => v.trim() === '' ? '0' : v). An empty or whitespace-only input transforms to '0'. The DB column is NOT NULL DEFAULT '0', so this is consistent.
actions: Clear the safety stock field (make it empty)
verify: Zod transforms empty string to '0'
Payload contains safetyStock: '0'
DB stores safety_stock = 0.0000

scenarios.name: Non-numeric safety stock passes Zod and fails at Postgres
scenarios.oracle: safetyStock transform only handles empty→'0'. A non-empty non-numeric string like 'abc' passes through untouched and reaches Postgres numeric(12,4), which rejects it.
verify: Zod transforms: 'abc'.trim() !== '' so value stays 'abc'
Payload contains safetyStock: 'abc'
Postgres rejects: invalid input syntax for type numeric

scenarios.name: Negative stock is rejected by Zod refine on create
scenarios.oracle: Stock has z.string().refine(v => !isNaN(Number(v)) && Number(v) >= 0). A negative value like '-5' must be rejected client-side before reaching the API.
verify: Zod rejects with 'Must be a non-negative number'
No fetch call is made to /api/items
Form shows field-level error on stock

scenarios.name: Non-numeric stock is rejected by Zod refine
scenarios.oracle: Stock refine checks !isNaN(Number(v)). The string 'abc' produces NaN, which fails the refine.
verify: Zod rejects with 'Must be a non-negative number'
No fetch call is made

scenarios.name: Stock of '0' on create does not create a lot or stock movement
scenarios.oracle: createItemWithLot only creates a lot when parseFloat(stock) > 0. Stock '0' means parseFloat('0') === 0, which is falsy via > 0, so no lot is created.
verify: Item is created in items table
No row is created in lots table for this item
No row is created in stock_movements table
Stock query returns 0 (COALESCE(SUM, 0))

scenarios.name: Positive stock on create creates a lot with purchase price as costPerUnit
scenarios.oracle: When stock > 0 on create, createItemWithLot creates a lot with quantity = stock and costPerUnit = defaultPurchasePrice. The purchase price is used as the initial lot cost.
verify: Item is created in items table with defaultPurchasePrice = 25.5000
Lot is created with quantity = '100' and costPerUnit = '25.50'
Stock movement is created with quantity = '100'
Lot has an auto-generated lot number (LOT-XXXXXX)

scenarios.name: Positive stock on create without purchase price sets lot costPerUnit to null
scenarios.oracle: When defaultPurchasePrice is null (empty field), the lot is created with costPerUnit = null because the DAL uses data.defaultPurchasePrice ?? null.
verify: Lot is created with costPerUnit = NULL
defaultPurchasePrice on item is NULL

scenarios.name: Increasing stock on update creates a new lot via adjustStockInTx
scenarios.oracle: On update, the API computes delta = newStock - currentStock. A positive delta creates a new lot and stock movement. The new lot does NOT carry the purchase price (adjustStockInTx doesn't set costPerUnit).
verify: API computes delta = 25 - 10 = 15
New lot is created with quantity = '15' and NO costPerUnit
Stock movement is created with quantity = '15'
Total stock (SUM of lots) = 25

scenarios.name: Decreasing stock on update deducts FIFO from existing lots
scenarios.oracle: On update, a negative delta triggers fifoDeduct which deducts from lots ordered by receivedAt (oldest first). Each deduction creates a negative stock movement.

setup.initialData: Existing item with stock = 20 across two lots (LOT-1: 12, LOT-2: 8)

verify: API computes delta = 5 - 20 = -15
fifoDeduct deducts 12 from LOT-1 (oldest), then 3 from LOT-2
LOT-1 quantity = 0, LOT-2 quantity = 5
Two negative stock movements created: -12 and -3
Total stock = 5

scenarios.name: Reducing stock below available amount returns insufficient stock error
scenarios.oracle: fifoDeduct throws 'Insufficient stock' when the requested deduction exceeds total available. The API catches this and returns { errors: { stock: ['Insufficient stock...'] } } with 400 status.
actions: Change stock from '5' to '0' (or any value requiring deduction > available)
verify: API computes delta = 0 - 5 = -5
fifoDeduct verifies total available >= 5
If available < 5 (e.g., some stock committed), throws 'Insufficient stock'
API returns 400 with { errors: { stock: ['Insufficient stock. Available: X, requested: 5'] } }
Transaction rolls back — no partial changes to item or lots

scenarios.name: Description: null, undefined, empty string, and whitespace all normalize to null
scenarios.oracle: nullableString accepts string | null | undefined. null/undefined → null. Empty string or whitespace → trim → empty → null. All three input forms produce null in the payload.
actions: Test 1: Leave description untouched (undefined from form)
verify: All three produce description: null in the Zod output
DB stores description = NULL

scenarios.name: BOM mode switch from quantity to percentage leaves stale quantity values in payload
scenarios.oracle: Switching BOM mode does NOT clear the inactive field's values. Quantity values entered in quantity mode persist in form state after switching to percentage mode. The submit payload contains both stale quantity and new percentage values.
actions: Add an ingredient, select a component, enter quantity '5.5'
Enter percentage '100' for the same row
verify: Payload bom[0] contains BOTH quantity: '5.5' AND percentage: '100'
bomRefine only validates the active field (percentage) — stale quantity is ignored
Both values are written to bom_components table
DB row has quantity = 5.5000 AND percentage = 100.00

scenarios.name: BOM mode switch from percentage to quantity leaves stale percentage values in payload
scenarios.oracle: Switching from percentage to quantity mode does NOT clear percentage values. The submit payload contains stale percentage alongside new quantity values.
actions: Add an ingredient, select a component, enter percentage '50'
Enter quantity '10' for the same row
verify: Payload bom[0] contains BOTH quantity: '10' AND percentage: '50'
bomRefine only validates quantity — stale percentage passes unchecked
Both values are written to bom_components table

scenarios.name: Duplicate component in BOM is rejected by bomRefine
scenarios.oracle: bomRefine checks for duplicate componentId values in the bom array. Selecting the same component in two rows must produce a 'Duplicate component' error on the second row.
actions: Select the same component (componentA) in both rows
verify: Zod bomRefine detects duplicate componentId
Error 'Duplicate component' is added to path ['bom', 1, 'componentId']
Form does NOT submit — no fetch call made
The first row has no error; only the second (duplicate) row shows the error

scenarios.name: BOM row with empty component is rejected on submit
scenarios.oracle: Each BOM row's componentId uses z.string().min(1). An empty componentId (default when row is added) must fail validation with 'Component is required'.
actions: Click '+ Add Ingredient' to add an empty row
verify: Zod rejects with 'Component is required' on bom[0].componentId
No fetch call is made
Error is displayed below the component combobox

scenarios.name: BOM quantity is required when bomMode is 'quantity'
scenarios.oracle: bomRefine checks: if bomMode === 'quantity' && !row.quantity, add error. nullableString transforms empty/whitespace to null, so an empty quantity field triggers this check.
actions: Add an ingredient and select a component
verify: nullableString transforms empty quantity to null
bomRefine detects bomMode='quantity' with null quantity
Error 'Quantity is required' at path ['bom', 0, 'quantity']
No fetch call is made

scenarios.name: BOM percentage is required when bomMode is 'percentage'
scenarios.oracle: bomRefine checks: if bomMode === 'percentage' && !row.percentage, add error. Empty percentage input is normalized to null by nullableString, triggering the required check.
actions: Add an ingredient and select a component
verify: nullableString transforms empty percentage to null
bomRefine detects bomMode='percentage' with null percentage
Error 'Percentage is required' at path ['bom', 0, 'percentage']
No fetch call is made

scenarios.name: BOM percentage total != 100% shows warning but does NOT block submission
scenarios.oracle: The PercentageTotal component shows a red warning when percentages do not sum to 100%, but this is COSMETIC ONLY. There is no Zod validation for percentage sum. The form submits successfully.
actions: Add two ingredients with components selected
Enter percentage '30' for row 1 and '20' for row 2 (total: 50%)
verify: UI shows total '50.0%' in red with '(should be 100%)'
Form submits successfully — Zod has no sum validation
API accepts the payload and stores both percentages
DB has percentage = 30.00 and percentage = 20.00 in bom_components

scenarios.name: Non-numeric BOM quantity passes Zod and fails at Postgres
scenarios.oracle: BOM quantity uses nullableString — only trims and null-converts. A non-empty non-numeric string like 'abc' passes Zod and is sent to Postgres numeric(12,4), which rejects it.
actions: Add an ingredient, select a component
verify: nullableString trims 'abc' — non-empty, so it stays as 'abc'
bomRefine checks !row.quantity — 'abc' is truthy, so it passes
Payload contains bom[0].quantity: 'abc'
Postgres rejects: invalid input syntax for type numeric

scenarios.name: BOM percentage exceeding numeric(5,2) precision fails at Postgres
scenarios.oracle: BOM percentage is numeric(5,2), allowing max 999.99. A value like '1000' exceeds this precision. Zod has no numeric or range validation, so it passes to the DB.
actions: Add an ingredient, select a component
verify: Zod passes — no numeric range check
Payload contains bom[0].percentage: '1000'
Postgres rejects: numeric field overflow for numeric(5,2)

scenarios.name: Self-referencing BOM is blocked by API route check on update
scenarios.oracle: The PUT /api/items/[id] handler checks if any bom row has componentId === id. If so, it returns 400 with { errors: { bom: ['An item cannot reference itself as a component'] } }. This is also enforced by a DB CHECK constraint.
actions: Select the current product (prod-1) as the component
verify: Zod validation passes — no self-reference check in schema
API route detects componentId === id
API returns 400 with { errors: { bom: ['An item cannot reference itself as a component'] } }
No database changes are made

scenarios.name: Updating a non-existent or deleted item returns 404
scenarios.oracle: updateItem queries with eq(items.id, id) AND isNull(items.deletedAt). If no row matches (wrong ID or soft-deleted), it returns null, and the API returns 404 with { error: 'Item not found' }.
verify: DAL updateItem returns null
API returns 404 with { error: 'Item not found' }
No database changes are made

scenarios.name: Duplicate SKU within same org is rejected by partial unique index
scenarios.oracle: The partial unique index items_org_sku_uidx enforces uniqueness on (organization_id, sku) WHERE sku IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. Two active items with the same non-null SKU in the same org will cause a unique constraint violation.

setup.initialData: Another active item with sku = 'MAT-001' already exists

verify: Zod validation passes — no uniqueness check in schema
API inserts into items table
Postgres rejects with unique constraint violation on items_org_sku_uidx
API returns 500 (unhandled DB constraint — no specific error mapping)

scenarios.name: Update schema omits itemType and unitDefinitionId — they are immutable
scenarios.oracle: updateItemSchema omits itemType and unitDefinitionId. Even if these fields are somehow included in the request body, they will be stripped by Zod .omit(). The item's type and unit cannot change after creation.
actions: Submit update with body containing itemType: 'material' and unitDefinitionId: 'new-unit-id'
verify: Zod strips itemType and unitDefinitionId from parsed output
DAL receives data without these fields
Item's itemType and unitDefinitionId remain unchanged in DB

scenarios.name: BOM update deletes all existing rows and re-inserts new ones
scenarios.oracle: updateItem always deletes all bomComponents for the item, then re-inserts the new set. This means removing a component is implicit (just don't include it in the new array). If bom is undefined, no BOM changes are made.
verify: API receives bom array with 2 rows
DAL deletes ALL 3 existing bom_components rows for this item
DAL inserts 2 new bom_components rows
The removed component is no longer in bom_components
The modified quantity is stored in the new row

scenarios.name: Create form default values include all fields to prevent undefined in Zod
scenarios.oracle: The create form must set defaultValues for ALL fields, including optional ones with null. Missing defaults cause undefined values that may not match the Zod schema expectations.
actions: Render form in create mode without touching any field
verify: name defaults to '' → fails min(1)
unitDefinitionId defaults to '' → fails min(1)
stock defaults to '0' → passes refine
safetyStock defaults to '0' → transform keeps '0'
bomMode defaults to 'quantity'
bom defaults to []
sku, category, description, defaultPurchasePrice, defaultSellingPrice are undefined (not in create defaults) → nullableString handles undefined via .nullable()

scenarios.name: Edit form converts Postgres numeric strings to parseFloat for display
scenarios.oracle: In edit mode, defaultPurchasePrice and defaultSellingPrice are converted via String(parseFloat(value)) to strip trailing zeros. Stock and safetyStock use the same pattern. '25.5000' becomes '25.5'.
verify: Purchase price input shows '25.5' (not '25.5000')
Stock input shows '100' (not '100.0000')
Safety stock input shows '10' (not '10.0000')
Submitting without changes produces the cleaned string values

scenarios.name: Deleting an item used as a BOM component is rejected
scenarios.oracle: deleteItem checks if the item is referenced in bomComponents of any active (non-deleted) item. If so, it returns { deleted: false, usedInBom: true }, and the API returns 400.

setup.initialData: Material used as component in a product's BOM

verify: DAL finds a bom_components row referencing this item
DAL returns { deleted: false, usedInBom: true }
API returns 400 with { error: 'Cannot delete: this item is used as a component in other products.' }
Item is NOT soft-deleted — deletedAt remains NULL

scenarios.name: BOM component FK uses ON DELETE RESTRICT — prevents hard-deleting referenced items
scenarios.oracle: bom_components.component_id references items(id) with ON DELETE RESTRICT. Even if the soft-delete check is bypassed, a hard-delete of an item used as a component would be blocked by the FK constraint.

setup.initialData: Material referenced as component in bom_components

actions: Attempt hard DELETE from items table (bypassing soft-delete)
verify: Postgres rejects with FK violation: cannot delete from items because bom_components still references it
ON DELETE RESTRICT is the safety net behind the application-level usedInBom check

scenarios.name: Clearing category sets form value to null via onValueChange callback
scenarios.oracle: The category combobox's onValueChange is (v) => field.onChange(v || null). When the value is cleared (v = ''), it becomes null. nullableString then passes null through as null.
verify: field.onChange receives null (not empty string)
nullableString receives null and returns null
Payload contains category: null
DB stores category = NULL

scenarios.name: Stock unchanged on update skips lot operations entirely
scenarios.oracle: When delta === 0 (new stock equals current stock), adjustStockInTx is NOT called. No lots are created or modified, and no stock movements are recorded.
verify: API computes delta = 10 - 10 = 0
adjustStockInTx is NOT called
No new lots or stock movements are created
Item metadata (name) is updated successfully

scenarios.name: Complete product creation with BOM, stock, pricing — full pipeline
scenarios.oracle: A complete product creation populates items, lots, stock_movements, and bom_components tables. All field transforms are applied. The lot uses purchase price as costPerUnit.
actions: Add 3 ingredients with components and quantities
verify: Item created in items table with all fields populated correctly
name = 'Concrete Mix 40kg', sku = 'PROD-001', category = 'Concrete'
description = 'Pre-mixed concrete bag'
defaultPurchasePrice = 12.5000, defaultSellingPrice = 24.99
safetyStock = 50.0000, bomMode = 'quantity'
Lot created with quantity = '200', costPerUnit = '12.50'
Stock movement created with quantity = '200'
3 bom_components rows created with correct componentId and quantity values
API returns 201 with { id: '...' }

scenarios.name: Name longer than 255 chars passes Zod but may fail at DB
scenarios.oracle: Zod only checks min(1) for name. A 256-character name passes schema validation but violates the varchar(255) DB constraint.
actions: Enter a 256-character string in name field
verify: Zod validation passes — min(1) only checks minimum
Postgres rejects with varchar(255) constraint violation

scenarios.name: Purchase price update does NOT retroactively change existing lot costs
scenarios.oracle: On create, defaultPurchasePrice is used as costPerUnit for the initial lot. On update, changing purchase price only updates the items table — existing lots retain their original costPerUnit. New lots from stock increase have NO costPerUnit.

setup.initialData: Item with purchasePrice='10.00', existing lot costPerUnit='10.00'

actions: Increase stock by 5 (triggers new lot creation)
verify: items.defaultPurchasePrice updated to '20'
Original lot retains costPerUnit = 10.0000 (unchanged)
New lot (from stock increase) has costPerUnit = NULL (adjustStockInTx does not set it)
Purchase price change is metadata-only on update

scenarios.name: Stock field is optional in update schema — omitting it skips stock operations
scenarios.oracle: updateItemSchema makes stock optional. If the parsed stock is undefined, the API passes undefined to updateItem, which checks stock != null before doing any lot operations. Omitting stock means no stock change.
actions: Send PUT request with body that includes name but NOT stock
verify: Zod parses stock as undefined (optional field not provided)
API passes undefined to updateItem
updateItem skips the stock adjustment branch entirely
No lots or stock movements are created or modified
Item metadata is updated

scenarios.name: Product with no BOM rows submits bom as empty array
scenarios.oracle: A product form with no ingredient rows sends bom: [] in the payload. bomRefine returns early when bom.length === 0. On update, this triggers deletion of ALL existing bom_components for the item.
verify: Payload contains bom: []
bomRefine returns immediately (length 0) — no validation errors
DAL deletes all existing bom_components for this item
No new bom_components rows are inserted
Product now has no BOM
